{{short description|none}}
{{use dmy dates|date=February 2026}}
{{row hover highlight}}
In the years running up to the [[next Italian general election]], which will occur no later than 22 December 2027,{{efn|While [[elections in Italy]] are customarily held on a Sunday or Sunday and Monday, there is no constitutional requirement to do so; the latest possible date for a general election to be held is the 70th day following the expiration of the Parliament's five-year term. See {{cite web|url=http://www.senato.it/documenti/repository/istituzione/costituzione_inglese.pdf|url-status=live|title=Constitution of the Italian Republic|publisher=Parliamentary Information, Archives and Publications Office of the Senate Service for Official Reports and Communication|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901053655/https://www.senato.it/documenti/repository/istituzione/costituzione_inglese.pdf|archive-date=1 September 2022|access-date=19 February 2022}}}} various organisations are carrying out opinion polls to gauge voting intention in [[Italy]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://tg24.sky.it/politica/2022/10/14/ultimi-sondaggi-politici-pd-m5s-lega-fdi-fi|title=Sondaggi, dopo elezioni crescono FdI e M5s, Pd e Lega in calo|work=Sky TG24|language=it|date=14 October 2022|access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Massaro|first=Barbara|date=18 October 2022|url=https://www.panorama.it/news/ultimi-sondaggi-politica-voto-lega-m5s-pd-forza-italia-voto-elezioni|title=Gli ultimi sondaggi: le intenzioni di voto|work=Panorama|language=it|access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref>{{efn|The date range is from after the [[2022 Italian general election]], held on 25 September, to the present day {{as of|2026|07|lc=y}}. Poll results are reported at the dates when the fieldwork was done, as opposed to the date of publication; if such date is unknown, the date of publication is given instead.}} Under the Italian ''par condicio'' (equal conditions) law, publication of opinion polls is forbidden in the last two weeks of an electoral campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.agcom.it/diffusione-dei-sondaggi|url-status=live|title=Diffusione dei sondaggi|publisher=AGCOM|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220907102045/https://www.agcom.it/diffusione-dei-sondaggi|archive-date=7 September 2022|access-date=3 November 2022}}</ref>

=== Polling with parties of different years ===
==== Historical parties ====
In February 2025, BiDiMedia released a poll asking respondents how they would vote if political parties from different periods of Italian history were present in contemporary Italy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/portfolio/politiche-25-febbraio-2025/|title=Politiche 25 Febbraio 2025|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|date=25 February 2025|access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://agenparl.eu/2025/03/02/sondaggio-bidimedia-barbera-prc-se-si-votasse-oggi-con-i-partiti-presenti-nel-1921-25-i-comunisti-vincerebbero-le-elezioni/|title=Sondaggio BIDIMedia, Barbera (Prc): 'Se si votasse oggi con i partiti presenti nel 1921-25, i comunisti vincerebbero le elezioni!'|website=Agenparl|language=it|date=2 March 2025|access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025">{{cite AV media|last1=Mena|first1=Achille|last2=Regiroli|first2=Lorenzo|date=26 February 2025|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w4nHhEL_rYM|title=Il nuovo sondaggio BiDiMedia: tutti i voti a febbraio 2025|language=it|publisher=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|access-date=18 September 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref> The scenarios concerned the parties that contested the [[1921 Italian general election]], the [[1983 Italian general election]], and the [[2001 Italian general election]].<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025">{{cite web|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/2025/02/25/scenari-politici-e-scenari-storici-25-febbraio-2025/|title=Il nuovo sondaggio BiDiMedia: tutti i voti a Febbraio 2025|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|date=20 May 2025|access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref> In the first scenario, referring to the political parties of 1921, the [[Communist Party of Italy]] (PCd'I) received 20.2%, followed by the [[Italian Socialist Party]] (PSI) at 19.7%, the [[Italian People's Party (1919)|Italian People's Party]] (PPI) at 15.8%, [[Liberals (Italy)|Liberals]] (L) at 14.5%, and the [[National Bloc (Italy, 1921)|National Bloc]] (BN) at 13.1%, despite the latter including [[Benito Mussolini]] and [[Italian fascists]].<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The [[Italian Republican Party]] (PRI) received 9.9%, while the [[Italian Democratic Liberal Party]] (PLDI), the [[Reformist Democratic Party (Italy)]] (PRD), and [[Social Democracy (Italy, 1922)|Social Democracy]] (DS) respectively received 4.2%, 1.4%, and 1.2%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> According to this hypotetical vote, the parties supporting the governments formed after the election (PPI, L, BN, PLDI, DS, and PRD) would together account for 50.2%, compared with approximately 63.9% for the corresponding parties in the real election.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> Taken together, the left-wing bloc of the PCd'I and PSI accounted for 39.9% of the hypothetical vote.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> A broader left-wing bloc including the PPI would reach 55.7%, while the PCd'I, PSI, and PRI together would account for 49.8%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> On the right, L and BN together accounted for 27.6%, rising to 43.4% if the PPI is included.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/>

In the second scenario, referring to the political parties of 1983, the [[Italian Communist Party]] (PCI) received 22.2%, followed by [[Christian Democracy (Italy)|Christian Democracy]] (DC) at 20.8%, the [[Italian Social Movement]] (MSI) at 18.3%, and the PSI at 12.8%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The [[Italian Liberal Party]] (PLI) received 8.8%, followed by the PRI at 5.0%, the [[Radical Party (Italy)|Radical Party]] (PR) at 4.7%, [[Proletarian Democracy]] (DP) at 3.4%, and the [[Italian Democratic Socialist Party]] (PSDI) at 2.7%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> [[Regionalism (politics)|Regionalist]] parties, such as the [[South Tyrolean People's Party]] (SVP), the [[Valdostan Union]] (UV), the [[Sardinian Action Party]] (PSd'Az), and the [[List for Trieste]] (LpT), totalled 1.4%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The five parties that formed the [[Pentapartito]] government—DC, PSI, PSDI, PRI, and PLI—would together account for 50.1% of the hypothetical vote, compared with 56.4% in the 1983 election.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> Taken together, the left-wing bloc of the PCI, PSI, DP, and PdUP accounted for 41.8% of the hypothetical vote, rising to 46.5% if the PR is included.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The centrist bloc of the DC, PRI, PLI, and PSDI accounted for 37.3%, while the MSI alone received 18.3%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The distribution also differed from BiDiMedia's 2019 poll using the parties of 1983, which was topped by the far-right MSI,<!-- https://www.tpi.it/politica/sondaggio-voto-oggi-1983-elezioni-prima-repubblica-20191129506680/ https://it.blastingnews.com/politica/2019/11/sondaggio-elettorale-coi-partiti-del-1983-msi-sarebbe-primo-davanti-al-pci-terza-la-dc-003025048.html https://www.radioradicale.it/scheda/592335/sondaggio-di-bidimedia-quali-partiti-del-1983-oggi-voterebbero-gli-italiani-intervista --> as the PCI increased from 18.9% to 22.2%, the DC from 17.4% to 20.8%, and the PSI from 12.5% to 12.8%, while the MSI declined from 19.6% to 18.3%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The PR fell from 7.0% to 4.7%, whereas the PLI increased from 6.0% to 8.8%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/>

In the third scenario, referring to the political parties of 2001, [[Forza Italia (1994)|Forza Italia]] (FI) received 23.5%, followed by the [[Democrats of the Left]] (DS) at 22.3% and [[National Alliance (Italy)|National Alliance]] (AN) at 15.0%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> [[Democracy is Freedom – The Daisy]] (DL) and the [[Lega Nord|Northern League]] (LN) each received 7.5%, followed by the [[Communist Refoundation Party]] (PRC) at 6.4%, [[Italy of Values]] (IdV) at 5.4%, [[The Sunflower]] (IG) at 3.4%, and the [[Bonino List]] (LB) at 3.0%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The [[Party of Italian Communists]] (PdCI) received 1.7%, while the [[White Flower]] (CCD–CDU) and the [[European Democrats]] (DE) respectively received 1.3% and 0.8%.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The 2001 scenario differs from the other two because the parties were originally organised into established electoral coalitions.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> Unlike the other two scenarios, applying the 2001 coalition groupings to the BiDiMedia 2025 hypothetical vote generally matched the real-election result.<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> The [[Centre-right coalition (Italy)|centre-right coalition]], then known as the [[House of Freedoms]] and represented by FI, AN, LN, and CCD–CDU, would together account for 47.3% (compared to the 49.6% of the real election) while the [[Centre-left coalition (Italy)|centre-left coalition]], then under the [[The Olive Tree (Italy)|Olive Tree]] name and represented by the DS, DL, IG, and the PdCI, would account for 34.9% (compared to the 35.0% of the real election).<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/> Including the PRC, which was not formally part of the Olive Tree but did not field candidates in the [[first-past-the-post]] constituencies for the [[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]] under a non-belligerence agreement with the Olive Tree, the centre-left coalition would account for 41.3% (compared to 40.0% when the PRC's 5.0% is added to the real-election result).<ref name="Mena & Regiroli 2025"/><ref name="BiDiMedia 2025"/>

==== First Republic parties ====
A May 2026 poll, conducted by Quorum/YouTrend for [[Sky TG24]] on the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the [[2 June 1946 institutional referendum]], reported several questions concerning Italy's political past and constitutional system.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://tg24.sky.it/politica/2026/05/29/sondaggio-youtrend-referendum-2-giugno|title=Sondaggio Youtrend per Sky TG24, crescono FdI e FN, in calo Pd e Lega. Le intenzioni di voto|work=Sky TG24|language=it|date=29 May 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> Among respondents who would vote in a hypothetical repetition of the 1946 referendum, 85% would choose the republic and 15% the monarchy.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.repubblica.it/politica/2026/05/30/news/sondaggio_referendum_repubblica_monarchia_2_giugno-425379527/|title=Sondaggio: a 80 anni dal referendum del 2 giugno gli italiani sceglierebbero ancora la Repubblica|work=La Repubblica|language=it|date=30 May 2026|access-date=13 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Isola|first=Giulio|date=1 June 2026|url=https://www.avvenire.it/attualita/oggi-la-repubblica-piace-all85-degli-italiani-mattarella-il-2-giugno-1946-fu-una-svolta_109132|title=Oggi la Repubblica piace all'85% degli italiani. Mattarella: il 2 giugno 1946 fu una svolta|work=Avvenire|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> On the [[Italian Constitution]], 69% considered it still current: 27% regarded it as fully up to date and not in need of changes, while 42% considered it broadly current but in need of minor amendments; 22% instead considered it partly or entirely outdated, and 9% did not express an opinion.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2026/05/29/sondaggio-monarchia-repubblica-costituente-notizie/8403440/|title=Sondaggio monarchia e Repubblica: il 15% degli italiani sceglie la monarchia|work=Il Fatto Quotidiano|language=it|date=29 May 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> A separate question on the election of a new [[Constituent Assembly]] to rewrite the Constitution found 45% in favour, 42% opposed, and 13% undecided.<ref>{{cite news|last=Magnani|first=Niccolò|date=2 June 2026|url=https://www.ilsussidiario.net/news/sondaggi-politici-2-giugno-45-vuole-cambio-costituzione-partiti-prima-repubblica-pci-batte-dc-pli-top/2968825/|title=Sondaggi politici 2 giugno: 45% vuole cambio Costituzione {{!}} Partiti Prima Repubblica: PCI batte DC, PLI top|work=Il Sussidiario|language=it|access-date=13 September 2026}}</ref> The poll also found that [[anti-fascism]] was considered the element that had most united Italians over the previous 80 years by 59% of centre-left coalition voters, compared with 18% of centre-right coalition voters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.destradipopolo.net/non-e-bastata-la-sconfitta-al-referendum-tra-gli-elettori-del-centrodestra-il-64-e-favorevole-allelezione-di-una-nuova-assemblea-incaricata-di-riscrivere-la-costituzione/|title=Non è bastata la sconfitta al referendum? Tra gli elettori del centrodestra, il 64% è favorevole all'elezione di una nuova Assemblea incaricata di riscrivere la Costituzione|website=Destra di Popolo|language=it|date=30 May 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref>

The same poll asked respondents which parties of the [[First Italian Republic]] they would vote for. The [[Italian Communist Party]] (PCI) received 25.4%, ahead of [[Christian Democracy (Italy)|Christian Democracy]] (DC) at 20.1% and the [[Italian Social Movement]] (MSI) at 14.3%, followed by the [[Italian Socialist Party]] (PSI) at 11.9%, the [[Italian Liberal Party]] (PLI) at 9.5%, the [[Radical Party (Italy)|Radical Party]] (PR) at 6.6%, the [[Italian Democratic Socialist Party]] (PSDI) at 5.4%, and [[Proletarian Democracy]] (DP) at 3.0%.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2026/06/01/sondaggio-prima-repubblica-partiti-italiani-antifascismo-oggi/8405456/|title=Sondaggio sulla Prima Repubblica: oggi il 25,4% voterebbe il Pci, il 20% la Dc|work=Il Fatto Quotidiano|language=it|date=1 June 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.liberoquotidiano.it/news/politica/47978458/sondaggio-youtrend-pci-in-testa-msi/|title=Sondaggio Youtrend: Pci primo partito, poi Dc, botto-Msi. Prima Repubblica, se si votasse oggi...|work=Libero|language=it|date=1 June 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> The preferences largely reflected modern party affiliations: the PCI received particularly strong support among AVS, M5S, and PD voters, while the MSI attracted substantial support among FdI voters.<ref name="Baldi 2026">{{cite web|last=Baldi|first=Francesco|date=1 June 2026|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.com/se-tornassero-i-partiti-della-prima-repubblica-il-pci-sarebbe-il-piu-votato/|title=Se tornassero i partiti della Prima Repubblica, il PCI sarebbe il più votato|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|access-date=13 September 2026}}</ref> Specifically, 68% of AVS voters, 39% of M5S voters, and 37% of PD voters said they would vote for the PCI, while 43% of FdI voters said they would vote for the MSI; among PD voters, 20% would vote for the DC and another 20% for the PSI.<ref name="Baldi 2026"/>

==== First Republic politicians ====
A March 2025 poll, conducted by BiDiMedia, asked respondents which politician of the First Republic they appreciated the most and who they would vote for Prime Minister.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/2025/03/25/nuovo-sondaggio-bidimedia-marzo-2025-pacifismo/|title=Il nuovo sondaggio BiDiMedia: quanto paga il pacifismo?|date=25 March 2025|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|access-date=27 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media|last1=Mena|first1=Achille|last2=Regiroli|first2=Lorenzo|date=25 March 2026|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJQmMhuzXmY&t=3518s|title=Sondaggio BiDiMedia Marzo – Il pacifismo fa guadagnare voti?|publisher=BiDiMedia|language=it|access-date=27 September 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.agenziagiornalisticaopinione.it/opinionews/bidimedia-telegram-bettino-craxi-il-politico-della-prima-repubblica-piu-apprezzato-secondo-un-sondaggio/|title=BiDiMedia (Telegram): Bettino Craxi il politico della Prima Repubblica più apprezzato secondo un sondaggio|work=Agenzia giornalistica Opinione|language=it|date=27 September 2026|access-date=27 September 2026}}</ref> [[Enrico Berlinguer]] of the PCI received 31.2%, followed by [[Aldo Moro]] of the DC with 26.9%, [[Bettino Craxi]] of the PSI with 18.6%, [[Giorgio Almirante]] of the MSI with 15.9%, and [[Giulio Andreotti]] of the DC with 7.1%.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/portfolio/politiche-25-marzo-politica-internazionale/|title=Politiche (25 Marzo) e Politica Internazionale|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|date=26 March 2025|language=it|access-date=27 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media|last1=Mena|first1=Achille|last2=Regiroli|first2=Lorenzo|date=27 September 2026|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebHYTCRZhp8|title=Quale politico della prima repubblica è più apprezzato? – I Sondaggio|publisher=BiDiMedia|language=it|access-date=27 September 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref>

=== Polling by football team supported ===
A September 2026 poll by BiDiMedia among voters—not including those under 18—found [[Juventus]] first with 16%, [[Inter Milan]] second with 12%, [[AC Milan|Milan]] third with 11%, [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] fourth with 7%, Roma fifth with 5%, and [[Fiorentina]], [[Torino FC|Torino]], and [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] sixth, while other clubs accounted for 11% and those supporting no team for 32%.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lanotiziaincomune.it/attualita/tifosi-e-urne-il-dato-sorprende-ecco-per-chi-voterebbero-gli-italiani-divisi-per-squadra/|title=Tifosi e urne, il dato sorprende: ecco per chi voterebbero gli italiani|website=La Notizia in comune|language=it|date=13 September 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Montesano|first=Tommaso|date=14 September 2026|url=https://www.liberoquotidiano.it/news/politica/49135748/la-mappa-politica-tifo-milano-destra-napoli-5stelle<!--  https://uploads.disquscdn.com/images/93624e4909b3ce37a7bf532dcd8314824154f3bea240b6779f00d565a7a6c7e5.jpg -->|title=La mappa politica del tifo: Milano a destra, Napoli 5Stelle|work=Libero|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcinternews.it/news/votano-tifosi-interisti-testa-testa-fdi-pd-1018415|title=Come votano i tifosi? Tra gli interisti è un testa a testa FDI-PD|website=FC Inter News|language=it|date=14 September 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> Politically, voters supporting Juventus were relatively split across the political spectrum, slightly more leaning towards the centre-right coalition parties but favouring moderates,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/2026/09/09/sondaggio-bidimedia-9-settembre-2026/|title=Sondaggio BiDiMedia – 9 settembre 2026|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|date=9 September 2026|access-date=13 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.calcioefinanza.it/2026/09/14/per-chi-votano-i-tifosi-club-serie-a/|title=Sondaggio: la mappa politica del tifo in Italia. Per chi votano i sostenitori dei top club di Serie A|website=Calcio e Finanza|language=it|date=14 September 2026|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> while those supporting Inter and Milan in particular were more right-leaning, with above-average results for FN.<ref>{{cite web|last=D'Ausilio|first=Domenico|date=14 September 2026|url=https://www.calcionapoli1926.it/ultimissime-calcio-napoli/voti-partito-napoli-inter-juve-milan/|title=Svelate le intenzioni di voto per squadra tifata: per chi voterebbero i sostenitori del Napoli|website=CalcioNapoli1926.it|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref> Supporters of Napoli and Roma, particularly those of Napoli, were more favourable to the centre-left coalition parties.<ref>{{cite web|last=Luna|first=Angela|date=14 September 2026|url=https://www.affaritaliani.it/sport/tifo-politica-voto-tifosi-serie-a.html|title=Milan, Inter, Juve o... Dimmi per chi tifi e ti dirò chi voti. Ecco l'orientamento politico dei tifosi|website=Affaritaliani.it|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sorianiello|first=Lorenzo|date=14 September 2026|url=https://www.calcionapoli24.it/notizie/come-votano-i-tifosi-in-italia-sondaggio-bidimedia-tra-politica-e-calcio-n698480.html|title=Come votano i tifosi in Italia? Sondaggio tra calcio e politica: a Napoli vince il PD|website=CalcioNapoli24|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Leva|first=Francesca|date=14 September 2026|url=https://www.ilnapolista.it/2026/09/per-i-tifosi-e-scontro-anche-in-politica-juve-inter-e-milan-votano-fratelli-ditalia-napoli-e-roma-pd/|title=Per i tifosi è scontro anche in politica. Juve, Inter e Milan votano Fratelli d'Italia, Napoli e Roma pd|website=Il Napolista|language=it|access-date=14 September 2026}}</ref>

In line with historical research, Juventus attracted support across the country, making it the most supported club in [[Northern Italy]] and respectively the second behind Roma and Napoli in [[Central Italy]] and [[Southern Italy]], more so than Inter and Milan, the only other clubs with a similarly national distribution.<ref name="Regiroli 2026">{{cite web|last1=Regiroli|first1=Lorenzo|date=9 September 2026|url=https://sondaggibidimedia.it/2026/09/09/sondaggio-bidimedia-9-settembre-2026/|title=Sondaggio BiDiMedia – 9 settembre 2026|website=Sondaggi BiDiMedia|language=it|access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="Mena, Regiroli & Gurreri 2026">{{cite AV media|last1=Mena|first1=Achille|last2=Regiroli|first2=Lorenzo|last3=Gurreri|first3=Arianna|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DKwiB2-7vTQ|title=Chi Vincerà Le Elezioni? – analisi con BiDiMedia Sondaggi|language=it|publisher=BiDiMedia|date=9 September 2026|access-date=13 September 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref> Napoli drew most of its support from [[Campania]] and Southern Italy, while Roma drew most of its support from the [[Lazio]] region and Central Italy.<ref name="Regiroli 2026"/><ref name="Mena, Regiroli & Gurreri 2026"/> For other clubs, such as Lazio, the sample was not large enough to provide results as reliable or robust as those for the other clubs;<!-- https://www.threads.com/@sondaggi_bidimedia/post/DdOI8pUDKww/no-e-perche-e-al-troppo-poco/ --><ref name="Regiroli 2026"/><ref name="Mena, Regiroli & Gurreri 2026"/> however, in line with other research, the available results showed a strong right-leaning tendency.<ref name="Regiroli 2026"/><ref name="Mena, Regiroli & Gurreri 2026"/><ref>{{cite AV media|last1=Gallo|first1=Alfonso Maria|last2=Mena|first2=Achille|date=10 September 2026|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iRiN8Q40wV8|title=Chi vince al Ballottaggio? Il Sondaggio BiDiMedia di settembre!|language=it|publisher=La Miniera|access-date=13 September 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref>
